metadata.scope: Sprint 1 = M1-M5 only: a signature-sensitive v2 interface hash + signature set + an isolated subprocess iface builder + an honest 4-class change classifier, all landed DARK (no binary emits a v2 hash, no registry record changes, no published package identity moves). NON-SCOPE, deferred to Sprint 2: wiring cmd/ailang/pkg_publish.go (M6), wiring cmd/registry-validator (M7), persisting interface_signatures end-to-end (M8), and the GCS registry backfill (M9).
metadata.estimated_effort: Sprint 1 = 4 days (M1 0.5d, M2 0.5d, M3 1d, M4 1d, M5 1d). Sprint 2 = 5 days. TOTAL HONEST = 9 days versus the design doc's claimed 4.
metadata.ordering_rule: Riskiest reversible thing first (M3, the subprocess builder), irreversible thing last (all registry writes are in Sprint 2, deferred). Every Sprint 1 milestone is independently committable, leaves the tree green, and is cleanly git-revertable at its boundary.
metadata.verification_method: Read-only source reads plus executed baselines at HEAD 66add3b48 in the planner worktree. Exit codes captured WITHOUT a pipe (cmd > /tmp/out 2>&1; rc=$?) because ${PIPESTATUS[0]} is silently empty in zsh. Every negative grep is paired with a known-positive control scoped to the same path in the same command.
metadata.gitignore_warning: THIS FILE IS GITIGNORED. `git check-ignore -v .ailang/state/sprints/x.json` returns rc=0 via .gitignore:82. A plain `git add` will NOT stage it. The controller must `git add -f` or accept that only the markdown sprint plan is committed.
metadata.build_assertion_trap: `go build ./...` is rc=1 on unmodified HEAD (cmd/wasm: 'function main is undeclared in the main package'). It MUST NOT be used as a gate. The narrow assertion used instead is `go build ./internal/pkg/... ./internal/messaging/... ./internal/iface/... ./cmd/ailang ./cmd/registry-validator`, measured rc=0 at base.
metadata.acceptance_command_form: Every acceptance command asserts on the `--- PASS:` line, never on the go exit code alone. Measured both directions in one session: a nonexistent test under the corrected form reports RED (while plain `go test -run X` reports rc=0 with '[no tests to run]'), and an existing test (TestClassifyChange) under the identical form reports GREEN. This also fails a t.Skipf, closing the FindAilangBinary stale-binary silent-skip hole (internal/testutil/ailangbin.go:74-79).
metadata.slow_gate_warning: `go test ./cmd/ailang/...` measured rc=0 in 311.052s. The design doc's AC9 names it unscoped. Every cmd/ailang acceptance command in this plan is scoped with -run '^Test...$'.
metadata.blocking_precondition_for_sprint2: The design doc's V-log #37 blast-radius measurement (how many published versions lack _smoke.ail and would newly be refused by the D7a publish gate) is UNVERIFIED and could not be measured from this session — the live registry is unreachable here. M6 and M9 must not ship before a human or later iteration runs it.

velocity.loc_note: 1490 = exact sum of the five Sprint-1 milestone estimates (impl ~720 + tests ~770). Deliberately test-heavy: the sprint's whole value is a hash whose sensitivity is pinned, so most LOC is package fixtures plus sensitivity/determinism/cancellation tests. The 4-day budget is gated by subprocess and timing correctness (M3), not typing volume.

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: AC table: AC1-AC9 and AC12-AC19 'Passes on unmodified HEAD? No — test does not exist.'
discrepancies_found.finding: FALSE. `go test -run <regex>` with a non-matching regex exits 0. Measured: `go test ./internal/pkg/ -run TestInterfaceHashV2_SensitiveToAddedExport > /tmp/ac1.txt 2>&1; rc=$?` gives rc=0 and 'ok ... [no tests to run]'. Control in the same session, a test that does exist: `go test ./internal/pkg/ -run TestInterfaceHash_` also rc=0. 16 of the 19 acceptance gates are therefore GREEN at base and can never go red; an executor could ship zero tests and report all-green. Compounded by internal/testutil.FindAilangBinary (ailangbin.go:49) calling t.Skipf on a stale binary (:74-79), which is also rc=0 — so the subprocess ACs would be green-by-skip on any machine with a stale bin/ailang, the repo's normal state.
discrepancies_found.action: Every acceptance command in this plan asserts the `--- PASS: <TestName>` line AND rc=0. Verified both directions: nonexistent test -> RED, existing test (TestClassifyChange) -> GREEN, same form, same session. This also fails a skip.

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: D7c: `pkg.BuildModuleIface(ctx, packageDir, modulePath) (*iface.Iface, error)` 'parses the returned canonical JSON, and returns the *iface.Iface'.
discrepancies_found.finding: NOT IMPLEMENTABLE. The canonical JSON renders each export's type as a string (FuncJSON.Type string, internal/iface/json.go:33) while iface.IfaceItem.Type is a *types.Scheme (internal/iface/iface.go:29). Reconstruction needs a string->Scheme parser and none exists: `grep -rn 'func.*FromNormalizedJSON|func.*ParseIface|func.*UnmarshalIface' internal/iface/` is empty (control, same file, the one-way direction: `grep -rn 'func (i \*Iface) ToNormalizedJSON' internal/iface/json.go` hits :46), and `grep -rn 'func ParseType|func ParseScheme' internal/types/ internal/parser/` is empty (control: `grep -rc 'func ' internal/types/types.go` = 41).
discrepancies_found.action: Signature corrected to `BuildModuleIface(ctx, packageDir, modulePath) (*iface.InterfaceJSON, error)`. Nothing downstream needs a *types.Scheme — the v2 hash and the signature set are pure functions of the canonical JSON. Strictly simpler than the design; removes a deserializer from scope.

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: D5 classification table: 'old side signatures ABSENT | any new side | U (unknown)'.
discrepancies_found.finding: As written this stalls EVERY cascade the day M3/M5 lands. Before backfill and before either binary is wired, no package carries a signature set, so every comparison is legacy-vs-legacy and returns U. U forbids auto-apply and routes to review, so the coordinator stops auto-applying anything for every package until backfill completes. That is the mirror image of the harm the doc set out to avoid: a confident-wrong 'patch' is replaced by a total review stall.
discrepancies_found.action: Classifier is a 2x2 on WHICH SIDES carry signatures, not a 1-D test on the old side. legacy/legacy -> today's hash-only A/C, byte-identical to current behaviour (not a fallback: it is the unchanged legacy path for a wholly-legacy comparison). legacy-old/v2-new -> U (the genuine transition window, D5's real case). v2/v2 -> A/B/C by signature diff. v2-old/legacy-new -> U. Preserves D5's non-negotiable (U is explicit, never a silent A) while bounding the blast radius to packages that actually crossed the migration boundary. Guarded by TestClassifyChange_BothLegacy_UnchangedBehaviour (M5-A1).

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: M1: 'canonical, alias-excluded serialization (reuse ToNormalizedJSON machinery minus TypeAliases)' feeding one subcommand that also backs outputInterface.
discrepancies_found.finding: ToNormalizedJSON deliberately EMITS aliases (internal/iface/json.go:29 `Alias string json:"alias,omitempty"`, populated at :91-92) and `ailang iface --compact` reads the field back (cmd/ailang/check.go:533). It exists because of M-IFACE-RECORD-FIELDS so an agent can build/destructure a record type from the compact interface instead of cat-ing the source. If internal-dump-iface emits alias-EXCLUDED JSON and outputInterface is refactored onto it as M1 instructs, that agent-facing capability is silently deleted.
discrepancies_found.action: internal-dump-iface emits the FULL normalized JSON, byte-identical to `ailang iface`. Alias exclusion moves one layer later into a pure projection iface.HashProjection(*InterfaceJSON) []byte that drops types[].alias. FIX-1's single-definition property is preserved. Guarded by M2-A5 (subcommand output must diff-clean against `ailang iface`) and M4-A7 (TestInterfaceHashV2_IgnoresTypeAliases).

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: M1: 'Refactor the CLI's outputInterface to call BuildModuleIface and os.Exit(1) on its error.'
discrepancies_found.finding: BuildModuleIface is a subprocess wrapper, so this makes every `ailang iface foo.ail` fork an `ailang internal-dump-iface` child — a per-invocation process fork on a hot, user-facing, agent-facing command, for zero safety benefit. FIX-1's isolation requirement is about the registry SERVER compiling UNTRUSTED uploads (main.go:70 ListenAndServe), not about a local user compiling their own source. It is also a recursion hazard if the subcommand is ever wired through the same helper.
discrepancies_found.action: Two functions, one definition. iface.BuildCanonicalJSON(ctx, packageDir, modulePath) ([]byte, error) is the IN-PROCESS single definition; internal-dump-iface is a thin main-side wrapper that prints it; pkg.BuildModuleIface is the SUBPROCESS wrapper used only by publish and the validator; outputInterface calls BuildCanonicalJSON directly. FIX-1 satisfied (still exactly one serialization) without the fork. Guarded by M2-A4 (golden byte-identity against the pre-refactor binary).

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: D4/FIX-1: the hidden subcommand 'dissolves' the two-binary drift problem; AC9 guards it.
discrepancies_found.finding: It dissolves CODE duplication, not VERSION SKEW. The publisher resolves its helper via os.Executable() (cmd/ailang/pkg_publish.go:156); the validator resolves via bare exec.Command("ailang", ...) from PATH (cmd/registry-validator/validate.go:76,95,116). In production those are different binaries at different versions — a deployed container image versus whatever the user installed. Any type-renderer change makes them emit different canonical JSON for the same source, so publisher and validator disagree about package identity: exactly the D4 harm. AC9 builds both binaries from one tree at one commit and is structurally incapable of observing skew.
discrepancies_found.action: Deferred to Sprint 2 M7 with a concrete guard: the canonical JSON carries the producing binary's version, and the validator COMPARES the publisher-submitted v2 hash against its own recomputation and rejects the upload with HTTP 400 on mismatch (loud failure per CLAUDE.md section 2) instead of silently overwriting it as main.go:214 does today. Guard: TestValidatorRejectsHashMismatch.

discrepancies_found.finding: `go test ./cmd/ailang/...` measured rc=0 in 311.052s — a 5-minute acceptance gate, named unscoped.
discrepancies_found.action: Every cmd/ailang acceptance command in this plan is scoped with -run '^Test...$'. The registry-validator suite is fine unscoped (measured rc=0, 3.117s).

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: Mutation table: 'TypeAlias excluded from v2 hash | re-enable the Alias field in the canonical serialization | TestXModAlias_DigestIgnoresTypeAliases goes RED'.
discrepancies_found.finding: INVALID MUTATION. TestXModAlias_DigestIgnoresTypeAliases calls b.computeDigest(...) directly (internal/iface/xmod_alias_digest_test.go:32,36) — the BUILDER's digest, which this sprint does not touch. It is untouched by any change to the new hash projection, so the mutant stays green and the guard is vacuous.
discrepancies_found.action: The alias-exclusion guard is a NEW test on the v2 hash: TestInterfaceHashV2_IgnoresTypeAliases (M4-A7). TestXModAlias* is retained only as an unrelated regression lock (measured GREEN at base: 2 `--- PASS: TestXModAlias` lines, rc=0).

discrepancies_found.doc_claim: D7c: 'context propagated into pipeline.Run'; D7b: module path -> file resolution.
discrepancies_found.finding: CONFIRMED, no refutation. pipeline.RunWithContext(ctx, cfg, src) exists at internal/pipeline/pipeline.go:154, and pipeline.Config.PackageDir exists at :94-96 overriding where ailang.toml/ailang.lock are found. discrepancies_found.action: No change required. Recorded so the executor does not re-derive.

features.description: internal/iface/hash_projection.go: HashProjection(*InterfaceJSON) ([]byte, error), a pure deterministic alias-dropping projection of the normalized interface JSON (per D4), plus SignatureSet(*InterfaceJSON) []string producing sorted module:name:signature strings. No compiler, no subprocess, no fixtures, no binary — pure functions over a struct, so the one decision the whole sprint rests on (what exactly gets hashed) gets the fastest possible feedback and is trivially revertible.

deferred_to_sprint_2.why_deferred: First user-visible behaviour change: publish refuses on a broken exported module (design D7a), with an UNMEASURED blast radius (design V-log #37 is UNVERIFIED and the live registry is unreachable from this session). Land behind AILANG_PKG_IFACE_V2=1, default off, until the radius is measured.

IRREVERSIBLE — registry writes. The moment cmd/registry-validator/main.go:214 emits a v2 hash, newly published packages carry a v2 identity. Must also carry the D6 version-skew guard: the validator compares the publisher-submitted hash to its own recomputation and rejects HTTP 400 on mismatch rather than silently overwriting.

IRREVERSIBLE — schema on published records. Threads interface_signatures through PackageMetadata (internal/pkg/registry_types.go:39 neighbourhood), PackageVersionInfo, lockfile, pubsub, coordinator SQLite rows and the Firestore converter — the 8 persistence points in the design's Conflict Surface.

IRREVERSIBLE — rewrites historical registry metadata. The design budgets 1 day; a resumable, checkpointed, retrying batch job over an object store with two distinct failure taxonomies (failed vs unbackfillable) is not a 1-day item, and the design's own FIX-2 requirements (AC18 bounded batch, AC19 checkpointed resume) each imply persistence plus a resume path. Blocked on the same V-log #37 measurement as M6.
